title: Composite token-latency index and failover redispatch dashboard buildout
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: Instrument and surface a Composite Token Latency Index (CTLI) that fuses token-level latency SLIs with admission/redispatch signals and circuit-breaker state to improve triage during multi-region failover and load-shedding events. Deliver a Grafana dashboard and a lightweight aggregation job that produces the CTLI timeseries and annotated event overlays for failovers, circuit transitions, and redispatch spikes.

Why: Existing token SLIs and admit metrics live in separate panels which makes incident triage slow when region spillback or redispatch occurs. A composite index (normalized, explained below) helps SREs and oncall rapidly distinguish between slow decode, admission throttling, and cross-region redispatch cascades.

Success criteria (measurable):
- CTLI produced in metrics pipeline with 1m resolution and <5s additional pipeline latency.
- Dashboard shows synchronized views: token p50/p95/p99, admission_rate, redispatch_rate, circuit_state transitions, kv_cache_hit_rate, and synthetic-probe p95.
- Oncall runbook updated with three clear playbooks mapping CTLI patterns to corrective actions (scale, failover, reduce batch size, rollback quantization).
- No more than 10% increase in metric cardinality cost due to new tags (see sampling plan).

Design decisions and definitions:
- CTLI is a weighted z-score aggregation: combine standardized token-p95, admission-latency-percentile, and redispatch-latency contribution with weights tuned by historical incident attribution. The index will be unitless and calibrated so that a >2.5 score triggers a medium-priority alert.
- Instrumentation tags: region, model_variant, priority_class, shard_id (coarse), route_key. Avoid high-cardinality user/customer ids.
- Sampling strategy: for token-level traces use deterministic 1/50 sampling for full traces, full aggregation for percentile windows. Use downsampled histograms for long-term retention.
- Circuit state events will be emitted as discrete events (open/half-open/closed) with timestamps to allow overlay on the CTLI timeseries.

Implementation plan (high level):
1) Add metric producers in serving runtime: emit redispatch_count, redispatch_latency_hist, admission_wait_hist, token_latency_hist (per shard coarse), and circuit_state events (ENG change set).
2) Pipeline: create a Stream job that computes standardized percentiles and writes CTLI to metrics store at 1m granularity. Add metadata tags for backfill alignment.
3) Dashboard: build a primary CTLI panel + correlation row (aligned time axis) showing token p50/p95/p99, admission rate, redispatch rate, circuit_state timeline, kv_cache_hit_rate, and synthetic probe latency. Provide quick links to trace ids sampled during anomalies.
4) Alerting & Runbook: tune alert thresholds in staging for two weeks using synthetic microbursts, then promote to prod. Update runbook with playbooks and escalation paths.

Telemetry cost & cardinality tradeoffs:
- We intentionally limit shard_id cardinality to coarse buckets (e.g., shard-1..shard-16) and cap model_variant to top 10. If we need per-model debugging, use on-demand trace sampling to avoid continuous cardinality explosion.
- If observed cardinality grows, fallback plan is to route high-cardinality labels to a low-retention index and keep CTLI on low-cardinality tags only.

Operational notes:
- This ticket coordinates with Dedicated routing team to ensure redispatch metrics are emitted when cross-region spillback occurs.
- We will run chaos experiments in staging (region ejection, network delay) to validate CTLI signal fidelity before production alerts.

Deliverables:
- Metrics producer changes (PRs) and deployment notes
- Stream aggregation job and schema for CTLI timeseries
- Grafana dashboard with annotated panels and drilldowns
- Updated oncall runbook + PDF export
- Postmortem template for CTLI-triggered alerts
